# task-47b0cad2: copy the marked panel across a divided grid

## Rule
A grid is partitioned by full-width/full-height uniform divider bands into equal rectangular panels. Identify the unique panel containing the pattern/markers (cells different from the ordinary panel background); copy that panel's **entire contents**, including its background cells, into every panel at the same local coordinates. Keep divider lines unchanged. Do not assume the source is always the top-left panel: locate it from the current input.

## Evidence
- Demo (11x5): color-2 dividers are column 2 and rows 3,7. The resulting panels are 3x2. The upper-left panel `[[6,6],[8,1],[1,1]]` is copied into all six panels. This establishes copying the whole tile, not only the non-background markers.
- Solved test (17x11): color-4 dividers are columns 3,7 and rows 5,11. Panels are 5x3. The distinctive tile is the middle-left panel (rows 6-10, columns 0-2): `[[1,1,7],[9,1,1],[1,7,1],[1,1,1],[1,1,1]]`. Its complete 5x3 pattern was copied into each of the nine panels. A prior wrong guess left the marker tile unchanged; the actual operation replicates it throughout.

## Procedure
1. Find full uniform divider rows/columns and determine equal panel sizes.
2. Inspect panels and select the one with the non-background pattern; its position may vary. In known evidence all other panels are uniform background.
3. Tile the selected panel into every panel, preserving local coordinates and all cells, including background.
4. Preserve divider bands exactly; validate dimensions, alignment, and row widths.

## Caution
If multiple panels contain competing patterns, background is ambiguous, or panels differ in structure, do not blindly select a source; request a demo. This rule is task-specific and supported by one demo and a correct test submission.
